name: Tackhead
hook: Sugar Hill's own former house rhythm section, rebuilt in London as a dub-industrial unit.

blurb.age7: Tackhead was made up of musicians who used to play on Sugar Hill Records' early hip-hop songs. Later they worked with Adrian Sherwood to make a darker, dub-style sound.
blurb.age13: Guitarist Skip McDonald, bassist Doug Wimbish, and drummer Keith LeBlanc had been Sugar Hill Records' in-house rhythm section, playing on early hip-hop records including 'The Message'. After Sugar Hill's decline, they reformed in London as Tackhead under Adrian Sherwood's production, fusing dub, funk, and industrial noise.
blurb.adult: Tackhead is a direct link between two labels already on this map: musicians who built Sugar Hill's house sound left as that label's finances collapsed and found a second creative life on On-U Sound, carrying a hip-hop rhythm section's muscle into dub-industrial production.

signatureTracks.title: Rebel Discharge Vs Tricky Kid
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The clearest fusion of the group's Sugar Hill-honed rhythm section with Sherwood's dub-industrial production.

signatureTracks.title: Question Time
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Political sample collage over the same rhythm section, showing the industrial side of the project's range.
